ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a cyclohexane ring, and the same substituted carbon on the ring is connected to a hydroxyl OH and connected to an aminomethyl side chain CH2NH2. On the right side is an independent nitrogen-oxygen-containing fragment, whose structure can be read as O=N-O-N=O. The figure has curved arrows and electron dots, but the question requires ignoring arrows. Reasoning: According to the specified method, starting from the nitrogen atom of the left aminomethyl group to write SMILES gives N-C-C, in which the second carbon is the substituted ring carbon. This ring carbon belongs to cyclohexane and can be written as C1CCCCC1, and adding a hydroxyl branch (O) on the same ring carbon therefore gives the left fragment as NCC1(O)CCCCC1. The right independent fragment O=N-O-N=O is written as O=NON=O. The two fragments are not connected to each other, so they are connected with a dot.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First ignore all curved arrows as instructed. Convert the left component by choosing the aminomethyl nitrogen as the SMILES start: write N-C-C, where the second carbon is the substituted ring carbon. Encode the cyclohexane ring from that carbon as C1CCCCC1, placing the hydroxyl substituent on the same ring carbon as (O), giving NCC1(O)CCCCC1. Then convert the separate right-hand fragment O=N-O-N=O as O=NON=O. Because the two structures are disconnected, join them with a dot to obtain NCC1(O)CCCCC1.O=NON=O.
